newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end lower after Thurs rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end lower after Thurs rally.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled on a down note Friday after bouncing within a narrow range following Thursday's rally in tandem with all other energy futures, market sources said.
"It's been really thin, but stayed strong," said one Northeast futures trader.
The November contracts finished the week at their highest levels since this summer.
"We're trading back and forth, testing the highs," said a New York-based futures broker, noting there were a few sizable block trades on early activity.

A combination of fundamental factors triggered Thursday's rise: several unplanned coal unit outages, a surge in natural gas prices, firm air-conditioning demand in the Southwest and anticipation of early heating demand in the Northwest.

Some players also cited Bonneville Power Administration's change in its pricing of energy as supportive for the market. The federal power marketing agency is offering electricity and transmission capacity as separate products.
November California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled off eight cents at $18.15 a megawatt hour (MWh), its highest level since July 31 at $18.50.
December COB ended down one cent at $19.24 after hitting a session low of $19.05. January 1997 COB finished unchanged at $18.05.
November Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down five cents at $17.25 a MWh after hitting as high as $17.65. The contract reached its highest level since August 2 at $17.70.
December PV finished down five cents at $17.70 after hitting a session high of $17.95.
NYMEX estimated 158 COB and 55 PV contracts were sold.
The latest forecasts showed the western U.S. would receive warmer to much warmer-than-normal weather next week.
